ActivePolicy.description: `GET /v1/policy/active`: the tenant's validated policy and where its bundle is.
ActivePolicy.title: ActivePolicy

AssignmentRef.description:
A role held at org scope, within one team, or - derived from CODEOWNERS, never
assigned by hand - for one repo (`derived` is then true).
AssignmentRef.title: AssignmentRef

AssignmentRequest.description:
`POST /v1/rbac/assignments`: give `email` (created in the caller's tenant if new)
`role` at org scope, or within `team`.
AssignmentRequest.title: AssignmentRequest

AuditEntry.description: One audit record exactly as hashed (spec §14.5).
AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry

ChainHead.description: The last event a chain holds: `seq` 0 and `hash` "" before the first.
ChainHead.title: ChainHead

CheckRequest.description:
`POST /v1/rbac/check`: may the caller (or `user`, needing `rbac.assign`) do
`permission` for the org, a team or a repo?
CheckRequest.title: CheckRequest

EffectivePermissions.description:
What the caller may do, as the server computed it: permissions granted at org scope,
per team, and per repo (derived maintainerships), plus each known repo's team. For
display and CLI hints only; authoritative answers come from `POST /v1/rbac/check`.
EffectivePermissions.title: EffectivePermissions

ImportRow.description:
One CSV row's outcome: `add`, `unchanged` or `error` (with `error` saying why).
`line` is the row's first line in the file (1 is the header).
ImportRow.title: ImportRow

IngestRequest.description:
`POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/events`: run ledger entries exactly as chained (Zyroflo's
format), in order; the server caps the count (`max_ingest_entries`).
IngestRequest.title: IngestRequest

IngestResult.description: What an ingest stored: new entries, replayed ones (no-ops), and the head after.
IngestResult.title: IngestResult

InviteInfo.description: An invite without its token (only the invitee's mail carries the link).
InviteInfo.title: InviteInfo

InviteRedeem.description: `POST /v1/invites/redeem`: the token from the invite link (its `#` fragment).
InviteRedeem.title: InviteRedeem

InviteRedeemed.description:
What a redeemed invite gives, once: a control-plane token and, when the deployment
issues them, a gateway proxy key.
InviteRedeemed.title: InviteRedeemed

KillState.description:
`GET /v1/killswitch/state`: the active switches that may apply to a run of the
caller's (the CLI decides per step), and how long the answer may be cached.
KillState.title: KillState

KillSwitchRequest.description:
`POST /v1/killswitch`: stop (`kill`) or hold (`pause`) the runs a scope names.
`scope_kind` `tenant` is the spec's global switch (no `scope_value`); `team` limits a
switch of any kind to that team's runs (a team lead must give their own team).
KillSwitchRequest.title: KillSwitchRequest

Me.description: `GET /v1/me`: who the token belongs to, in which tenant, and what they hold.
Me.title: Me

NotificationInfo.description: A queued, sent or failed mail (never its body).
NotificationInfo.title: NotificationInfo

OrgCheck.description:
One org check: `check` is rbac, killswitch, policy, pipeline, versions, concurrency
or budget.
OrgCheck.title: OrgCheck

PolicySource.description:
`PUT /v1/tenant/policy-source`: where the tenant's policy repo lives. A URL with
credentials is refused (git credentials are mounted per tenant, ND-15).
PolicySource.title: PolicySource

PolicySourceChanged.description: The tenant after a policy-source change, and the sync it triggered.
PolicySourceChanged.title: PolicySourceChanged

Problem.description:
An RFC 9457 problem document. `code` is a stable machine name
(`auth.invalid_token`, ...); `hint` is a next step the CLI prints as is. A problem never
echoes a submitted secret and never names another tenant.
Problem.title: Problem

ProxyKeyIssued.description: A new gateway proxy key, in this response only.
ProxyKeyIssued.title: ProxyKeyIssued

RepoInfo.description: A registered repo and the maintainers its CODEOWNERS names (ND-6).
RepoInfo.title: RepoInfo

RepoRegistration.description: `POST /v1/repos`: register a repo for a team (`agent.edit.repo` in that team).
RepoRegistration.title: RepoRegistration

RoleImportRequest.description:
`POST /v1/rbac/import`: role assignments as CSV text (`email,role,team,handle`).
A dry run (the default) only reports what applying would do.
RoleImportRequest.title: RoleImportRequest

RoleUpdate.description: `PUT /v1/rbac/roles/{name}`: create or replace a role's permissions.
RoleUpdate.title: RoleUpdate

RunPreflight.description:
The org checks' report. `registered`: every check passed and the run holds a slot.
`team_budget_remaining_usd` is None while the gateway does not measure it - never 0.
RunPreflight.title: RunPreflight

RunRegistration.description:
`POST /v1/runs`: the org checks before a run starts (spec §8.2), and the run's
concurrency slot when they pass. `pipeline_file` is the pipeline's path in the policy
repo (None for a repo-layer pipeline) and `pipeline_sha256` the hash of its bytes (D33);
`agents` (name@version), `models` and `backends` are what the run's steps resolved to.
`overlay_file` and `overlay_sha256` are the team's overlay applied to the pipeline, by
its policy repo path and the hash of its bytes (M2-23; None: no overlay), and
`pipeline_version` the version of the pipeline the team gets (M2-15).
`dry_run` runs every check and registers nothing.
RunRegistration.title: RunRegistration

RunSummary.description:
`GET /v1/runs/{run_id}`: a run as the control plane holds it (ND-11: PR links point
here until a web UI exists).
RunSummary.title: RunSummary

ServiceAccountIssued.description: The one response that carries the service account's token.
ServiceAccountIssued.title: ServiceAccountIssued

ServiceAccountRequest.description:
`POST /v1/service-accounts`: a team-scoped account that may only trigger runs. Its
token expires after `days` (required, at most 365: owner decision 75).
ServiceAccountRequest.title: ServiceAccountRequest

SyncOutcome.description:
What one policy sync did. `failed`: the repo could not be fetched (`problems` says
why, credentials scrubbed).
SyncOutcome.title: SyncOutcome

TenantRef.description: The caller's tenant, as the server derived it from the token.
TenantRef.title: TenantRef

TokenIssued.description: The one response that carries a token value; it is never shown again.
TokenIssued.title: TokenIssued

TokenRequest.description:
`POST /v1/tokens`: a new token for the caller (rotation). `days` defaults to the
longest lifetime the caller's kind allows (90 for people, 365 for service accounts).
TokenRequest.title: TokenRequest

WebhookIssued.description: The webhook path, carrying the new hook token: shown once, never again.
WebhookIssued.title: WebhookIssued

HTTPBearer.description: A control-plane token (`acp_...`) from `agentic login --for control-plane`

get.description: Liveness: the process answers. Never touches the database.

Readiness: the database answers, is migrated to this release and enforces tenant
isolation and insert-only evidence (fail closed unless relaxed for development).
Records after `after_seq`, oldest first. With `team`, only that team's records.

schema.title: Response List Audit V1 Audit Get

get.description: Recompute every hash and link of the tenant's chain; [] means intact.

post.description:
Use an invite once: a control-plane token for the invite's tenant and, when this
deployment issues them, a gateway key bound to the tenant, the person and their team.
Both are in this response only.

get.description:
The switches the caller may clear: every switch for `killswitch.global`, else the
ones limited to a team where the caller holds `killswitch.team`.

schema.title: Response List Switches V1 Killswitch Get

post.description: Stop (`kill`) or hold (`pause`) the runs the scope names, from their next check.

get.description:
The active switches that may apply to a run of the caller's with this team, repo and
pipeline: agent, model and backend switches are always included (the CLI decides per
step). Any authenticated user of the tenant may ask; user switches are the caller's.

delete.description: Clear a switch: held runs continue on `agentic resume`, killed runs stay killed.

get.description: Who the token belongs to, in which tenant, and the roles they hold.

schema.title: Response List Notifications V1 Notifications Get

get.description: The tenant's active policy version and where to download its bundle.

post.description: Sync the tenant's policy now (org `policy.edit.org`); 202 when a sync is running.

get.description: The tenant's policy versions, newest first, accepted and rejected.

schema.title: Response List Versions V1 Policy Versions Get

get.description: An accepted version's bundle (`git archive`, gzipped); `ETag` is its digest.

post.description: A push to the tenant's policy repo: sync that tenant after answering (R15).

schema.title: Response Webhook V1 Policy Webhook  Hook Token  Post

post.description:
Replace the caller's newest gateway key: the old one stops working at once (within
the gateway's key refresh), the new one is in this response only. A key whose
revocation is pending is never rotated back to life; a new key that cannot be recorded
is revoked again, so the gateway never holds a key the control plane does not know.

get.description: Assignments in the tenant (org `rbac.assign`), or in one team (`rbac.assign.team`).

schema.title: Response List Assignments V1 Rbac Assignments Get

post.description:
Give a person a role at org scope or in a team; the person is created in the
caller's tenant when new. Team leads assign only team-assignable roles in their team.

delete.description: Revoke an assignment. The tenant's last org admin cannot be removed.

post.description:
May the caller - or `user`, which needs org `rbac.assign` - do `permission` for the
org, a team or a repo? The authoritative answer the CLI relies on.

Org admins import any row; team leads rows of their own team (each row is checked
like a single assignment).

schema.title: Response List Roles V1 Rbac Roles Get

delete.description: Delete a custom role that nobody holds (org `rbac.assign`).

put.description:
Create or replace a role (org `rbac.assign`). Org admins always keep `rbac.assign`.
The caller's right is checked before the body (DF-417): without `rbac.assign` every
request is a 403, whatever it asks for.

post.description:
Register a repo for a team (`agent.edit.repo` there); its remote must match the
active policy's `allowed_repo_patterns`. Registering again is a no-op.

get.description: Who CODEOWNERS makes a maintainer of the repo, and what stays unresolved.

post.description: Fetch the repo's CODEOWNERS now (`agent.edit.repo` in the repo's team).

The org checks before a run starts; the run is registered (it holds a concurrency
slot) only when every check passes and `dry_run` is false. An old CLI is refused first
(426 `cli.too_old`).

get.description:
The run: who started it, its team, policy version and chain head. Readable by its
starter and by holders of `dashboard.view.team` or `audit.read.team` in its team.
The run's events exactly as received, after `after_seq` (for `agentic audit verify`).

schema.title: Response Get Events V1 Runs  Run Id  Events Get

post.description:
Append a batch of the run's chained events: verified entry by entry, stored all or
nothing; replayed entries are no-ops (`duplicates`).

get.description: The tenant's service accounts (org `rbac.assign`), or one team's (its team lead).

schema.title: Response List Service Accounts V1 Service Accounts Get

post.description: A new service account in `team` and its token (shown in this response only).

get.description: The caller's tenant: its name and policy source (never a credential).

put.description: Point the tenant at its policy repo and branch (org `policy.edit.org`), then sync.

post.description:
A new policy-repo webhook URL for the tenant (org `policy.edit.org`); the previous
one stops working. The token is in this response only (ND-14).

schema.title: Response Get Tokens V1 Tokens Get

post.description:
A new token for the caller in the caller's tenant (rotation). The value is in this
response only. `revoke_current` revokes the token that made the request. A service
token never mints one that outlives it: its expiry is what limits a leaked CI token.

delete.description:
Revoke one of the caller's tokens. Anyone else's token - in this tenant or another -
answers like a missing one.

put.description:
Set a person's host-qualified handles (org `rbac.assign`; ND-6: never self-declared);
every repo's maintainers are re-resolved against them.

post.description: Send a person a new invite (their earlier unused ones stop working).

End a person's access in one step (org `rbac.assign`, ruling P10): disabled (their
roles stop counting), every control-plane token and unused invite revoked, a `user:`
kill switch stopping their running work, and their gateway keys revoked - a key the
gateway cannot revoke now is pending and the worker finishes it.

delete.description:
Revoke every gateway key of a person (org `rbac.assign`). A key the gateway cannot
revoke now is `pending`; the worker finishes it. The keys are marked first and the
gateway called after that commit, holding no tenant lock (review F2).
